title: Introduce compatibility shim and staged acceptance tests for heterogeneous telemetry clients
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description:
Problem: Multiple telemetry clients (SDKs, CLI tooling, and internal API integrations) emit event envelopes that vary subtly: missing optional fields, differing enum token names, and alternate timestamp formats. Downstream pipeline transforms and analytics jobs sometimes break or silently drop fields when schema evolves, complicating alerts, cost accounting, and feature flags in the Console.

Goal: Build a lightweight compatibility shim in the telemetry gateway plus a staged acceptance-test harness that verifies SDK/CLI/API client behavior against our canonical analytics schema before rolling schema changes wide. The shim will normalize common variations and emit negotiation metadata for observability. The harness will run contract tests (unit + integration) with golden vectors and gate rollouts via a canary cohort.

Scope: gateway shim, schema negotiation headers, normalization rules for top-10 incompatibilities, contract-test harness that runs in CI and in a canary testbed, dashboards and SLOs for contract regression, rollout playbook for dark-run -> canary -> ramp.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway shim sits behind existing telemetry ingress and applies normalization without adding >5ms p50 latency for 99% of events
CI job fails when SDK/CLI change introduces a non-backwards-compatible breaking change unless a migration flag is present
Staged acceptance harness validates SDK/CLI/API against golden vectors and produces a pass/fail report accessible from the console-telemetry project page
Rollout plan documented and tested: dark-run, 1% canary, 10% ramp, full rollout — with automatic rollback on contract-failure metric
Dashboard tracking schema negotiation versions, normalization count by rule, and event drop rate (baseline)
technical_notes: Compatibility shim responsibilities: detect client-declared schema/version (x-telemetry-schema header), apply per-version normalization rules, tag events with negotiated_version and shim_actions (list), and forward to existing ingestion topic

Normalization rules prioritized from production logs (top-10): timestamp formats (iso vs unix ms), missing tenant_id defaults, legacy event_type enums mapping, base64 encoded payload vs json, truncated error.reason -> error.message mapping
Negotiation semantics: accept header values 'v1', 'v2', 'v2.1-preview'; if absent attempt best-effort normalization and tag as 'unknown-client' in metadata

Contract tests: consumer-driven contract approach. Define minimal canonical JSON schema and a set of golden vectors (50+) covering edge cases. Each SDK/CLI repo will run the contract suite in PRs via GitHub Actions and report status to the console-telemetry CI project

Staged harness: local unit mocks -> CI integration (sandbox ingestion cluster) -> canary testbed (1% traffic) -> ramped production. The harness must be runnable as a Docker image for parity testing on Dedicated/Private deployments

Metrics and alerts: metric 'telemetry.normalizations_total' labeled by rule, 'telemetry.schema_negotiation_failures', 'telemetry.event_drop_rate'; alert if normalization rate increases >3x baseline or drop_rate >0.5% for 15 minutes
Data pipeline implications: downstream transforms must accept shim tags and avoid double-normalization. Add a lightweight 'trusted' flag from shim to bypass legacy heuristics in the ETL
Backward compat: shim must be opt-out via client header 'x-telemetry-shim: disabled' for advanced customers testing migration paths
Privacy/security: shim must not enrich events with PII. Any field-mapping that could surface secrets must be blocked; security review required (see security_review_required=true)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Design doc and consensus — merge spec to Confluence and record in console-telemetry-v2
Stage 1: Implement shim as a feature-flagged sidecar in telemetry-gateway; unit tests for normalization rules
Stage 2: Add contract-test suite and integrated CI job across SDK/CLI repositories (proposal PRs: github.com/redwood/sdk-contracts)
Stage 3: Dark-run — run shim in pass-through mode with logging enabled for 48h, analyze normalization counts
Stage 4: Canary (1% production) for 72h with strict contract gating; auto-rollback on contract-failure metric
Stage 5: Ramp to 10% then 50% with manual checkpoint reviews; full rollout after two successful windows
Stage 6: Deprecation window for legacy schemas (announce 90 days) and final removal option behind enterprise toggle
